answer: Agents must bond a scarce token before joining, and a randomly selected peer checks each identity’s work over time. A false identity can imitate a signal, but it cannot cheaply multiply trusted votes: each new account locks another bond, while colluding accounts risk losing it when caught submitting inconsistent attestations. The glacier-like delay before a bond can be withdrawn makes rapid identity cycling costly; a lagoon of fresh accounts still needs capital and time to gain influence.
